narrative.overview: A high-volume, promotion-driven retail storefront for home connectivity on a disciplined enterprise token system. Clean neutral chrome (white surfaces, near-black text and buttons, generous whitespace) lets concentrated bursts of purple — gradient campaign bands, line icons, check-bullets, emphasis phrases — carry the brand while loud, time-bound offers do the shouting.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black primary actions; purple as a sparing brand accent, not the button color.
Signature purple gradient promo band with an oversized numeral.
Clean white / #f6f6f9 surfaces, hairline #dde2e6 borders, mostly flat.
Modular, card-based, long-scroll marketing pages with recurring system bands.

rules.name: The Black-Button Rule
rules.body: Primary conversion buttons are near-black (#141417), never purple. Purple is the brand's voice, not its action color.

rules.name: The Rare-Purple Rule
rules.body: Saturated purple appears on a small fraction of any screen; its scarcity against the neutral frame is what reads as Xfinity.

rules.name: The Two-Track Scale Rule
rules.body: The type scale runs on two ratios — display ~1.12 and headline ~1.20-1.25 — bridged by a larger jump.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Headings are sentence case; emphasis comes from size, weight, and a purple fragment, not capitalization.

rules.name: The Border-First Rule
rules.body: Separation is a hairline border before it is a shadow.

dos: Do keep primary actions near-black and reserve purple for brand voice (promo bands, icons, check-bullets, emphasis).
Do lead shopping surfaces with the address-capture step; it is the site's real hero.
Do build pages as stacked modular bands on a 4px spacing rhythm within a 1280px container.
Do use sentence case and let size/weight/a purple fragment carry emphasis.
Do separate surfaces with hairline #dde2e6 borders first, soft shadows second.
donts: Don't spread purple across large surfaces; its scarcity is the signal.
Don't ship images with empty alt text (a current-state gap on ~84% of images).
Don't rely on heavy drop-shadows as the default surface style.
